corrections.name: Velia: cut for Via dell'Impero (Via dei Fori Imperiali), 1931-32
corrections.note: Restore the removed ridge for every ancient year: crest +18 m on the road axis, tapering (cosine) to 0 at 30 m each side and over the last 30 m at each end. Fallback if 'ridge' is not implemented: +15 m over the inner 30 m strip and +7 m over the outer strips. The Velia crest at Villa Rivaldi stood c. 40 m before the cut; Via dei Fori Imperiali runs at c. 22-24 m here.
scholarship: Muñoz' cut: 200 m long, 60 m wide, 18-20 m deep (Roma 3.0 workshop / Sovrintendenza; Velia exhibition 2022)

corrections.name: Saddle between the Capitoline (Arx) and the Quirinal, removed for the Forum of Trajan
corrections.note: Before the Trajanic works (c. 106-112, perhaps begun under Domitian) a saddle joined the Arx to the Quirinal; the Clivus Argentarius (Via di Marforio) crossed it, 5 m wide at c. 10 % gradient. Crest elevations along the line, absolute m asl. The Julio-Claudian street under the column at 15.52 m shows the crest passed SE of the column. Fallback: +8 m over the polygon.
scholarship: Platner and Ashby, A Topographical Dictionary of Ancient Rome (1929) (Forum Traiani: ridge long assumed, but an early-imperial street lies under the column)
Lancaster, 'Building Trajan's Column', AJA 103 (1999) 419-439 (Julio-Claudian road under the column at c. 15.52 m asl)

corrections.name: Monte Testaccio (amphora dump)
corrections.note: ancient = baseAncient(y) + max(0, modern - baseModern) * scale(y) * (peakAncient - baseAncient)/(peakModern - baseModern). Dumping from the Augustan age (perhaps 1st c. BC) to the 260s, in terraces with amphora retaining walls; full height c. 35 m above the plain, 49-50 m asl, by c. 250. The DSM shows the mound smoothed to c. 26 m and TINITALY to c. 34 m; synthesize a terraced cone from the polygon and peak if needed. Delta form: keyframes give the change at the peak.
scholarship: Platner and Ashby, A Topographical Dictionary of Ancient Rome (1929) 512-513
